Topics · Hard times

Is there really wisdom in every hardship?

The Quran says less: ease with hardship, a partial view, and only the one who lived it may name any good.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا٥ إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease [i.e., relief]. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.

Quran · Ash-Sharh 94:5-6

Translation

Yahweh my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me. Yahweh, you have brought up my soul from Sheol. You have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit. Sing praise to Yahweh, you saints of his. Give thanks to his holy name. For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.

Original · Hebrew

יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֑י שִׁוַּ֥עְתִּי אֵ֝לֶ֗יךָ וַתִּרְפָּאֵֽנִי׃ יְֽהוָ֗ה הֶֽעֱלִ֣יתָ מִן־שְׁא֣וֹל נַפְשִׁ֑י חִ֝יִּיתַ֗נִי מִיָּֽרְדִי־בֽוֹר׃ זַמְּר֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חֲסִידָ֑יו וְ֝הוֹד֗וּ לְזֵ֣כֶר קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ כִּ֤י רֶ֨גַע ׀ בְּאַפּוֹ֮ חַיִּ֪ים בִּרְצ֫וֹנ֥וֹ בָּ֭עֶרֶב יָלִ֥ין בֶּ֗כִי וְלַבֹּ֥קֶר רִנָּֽה׃

the Psalms · 30:2-5

World English Bible

'Everything happens for a reason' is a bigger claim than these lines make. They say something narrower, twice: with hardship comes ease. The word here is with. The Quran also says after (65:7), but here ease is more than a prize at the end of the road. It is said to travel alongside. That may mean a friend who stays, a breath you did not expect, a strength you did not plan. The lines do not say how much, or when. A smaller claim is easier to test.

A question for you

Which line is nearest to what you have lived?

If you saySomething came with it, and I still would not choose it.
ThenBoth can be true. The hardship stays hard, and what came with it stays yours.
If you sayNot yet.
ThenThat word leaves a door open, and no one here will push it.
If you sayNo, and I am tired of being told so.
ThenYou may have heard it too often from people who were not carrying what you carry. The next part stands with you on that.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا٦٧ وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ خُبْرًا٦٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

He said, "Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience. And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?"

Quran · Al-Kahf 18:67-68

Now the honest difficulty. When we cannot see a reason, is there one? In a Quranic account, a man given knowledge tells Moses he will not be able to bear what he is about to see. Then comes a question close to tenderness: how could anyone hold steady under what their knowledge does not reach? The line does not blame the one who struggles. It says that not seeing is what makes it hard. So a person in the dark is not failing.

A question for you

When you cannot see a reason, which is closest to what you do?

If you sayI assume there is one I cannot see.
ThenThat is trust, and it has carried many people. It is a way of living with the question, and it does not close it.
If you sayI assume there is none.
ThenThat too is a way of living with it, and it has its own courage. Nothing here asks you to change it today.
If you sayI assume nothing. I wait.
ThenWaiting without a conclusion is harder than either. It is also what the account asks of Moses.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا۟ لَهُۥ سُجَّدًا ۖ وَقَالَ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ هَـٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُءْيَـٰىَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّا ۖ وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِىٓ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْبَدْوِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِىٓ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration.[618] And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle[619] in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.

Translator's notes

[618] That of greeting and respect, which was lawful until the time of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ). Prostration to any person or object other than Allāh was then prohibited conclusively. [619] Perceptive of unapparent matters within which is benefit to His servants.

Quran · Yusuf 12:100

Translation

For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest. God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance. So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

Original · Hebrew

כִּי־זֶ֛ה שְׁנָתַ֥יִם הָרָעָ֖ב בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְעוֹד֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־חָרִ֖ישׁ וְקָצִּֽיר׃ וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם לָכֶ֛ם שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּלְהַחֲי֣וֹת לָכֶ֔ם לִפְלֵיטָ֖ה גְּדֹלָֽה׃ וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹֽא־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִי֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְשִׂימֵ֨נִֽי לְאָ֜ב לְפַרְעֹ֗ה וּלְאָדוֹן֙ לְכָל־בֵּית֔וֹ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 45:6-8

World English Bible

So who may say that a hardship held some good? Look at who says it here. Joseph, after a well, after being sold, after prison, after long years away from his father, is reunited with his family and says that his Lord is gentle. He says it himself, about his own life, at the far end. No person says it to him in the well. That may be the rule: this sentence belongs to the one who lived it, if they ever come to say it.

A question for you

If someone near you is in hardship today, which would you reach for?

If you sayA reason that might comfort them.
ThenThere is love behind that. You might first find out whether they want a reason.
If you sayMy presence, and very few words.
ThenThat is the thing a page cannot do.
If you sayI do not know what to do.
ThenFew people do. Saying exactly that to them is often a true place to begin.

The same in the other books

Translation

Those who sow in tears will reap in joy. He who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with joy, carrying his sheaves.

Original · Hebrew

הַזֹּרְעִ֥ים בְּדִמְעָ֗ה בְּרִנָּ֥ה יִקְצֹֽרוּ׃ הָ֘ל֤וֹךְ יֵלֵ֨ךְ ׀ וּבָכֹה֮ נֹשֵׂ֪א מֶֽשֶׁךְ־הַ֫זָּ֥רַע בֹּֽ֬א־יָב֥וֹא בְרִנָּ֑ה נֹ֝שֵׂ֗א אֲלֻמֹּתָֽיו׃

the Psalms · 126:5-6

World English Bible

Translation

For the Lord will not cast off forever. For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses. For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יִזְנַ֛ח לְעוֹלָ֖ם אֲדֹנָֽי׃ כִּ֣י אִם־הוֹגָ֔ה וְרִחַ֖ם כְּרֹ֥ב חֲסָדָֽיו׃ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עִנָּה֙ מִלִּבּ֔וֹ וַיַּגֶּ֖ה בְנֵי־אִֽישׁ׃

Lamentations · 3:31-33

World English Bible

Translation

It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes.

טֽוֹב־לִ֥י כִֽי־עֻנֵּ֑יתִי לְ֝מַ֗עַן אֶלְמַ֥ד חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃

the Psalms · 119:71

Your reflection

Is there a sentence about your own hard road that only you could say? Have you said it, or is it still too early?
